Final experiment design — design-only deliverable. No code executed; no experiment claimed to have run. Per the controller convention this is the substantive content ("payload") and the message field is the brief pointer above.

================================================================
Title: Fused Adam (TorchOpt) vs Unfused Adam — Gradient/Compute Graph Complexity and Interpretability
================================================================

1. Research question (restated). Does fusing operations within the Adam optimizer (as done in TorchOpt) result in a less complex and more interpretable gradient graph compared to the output from TorchViz?

2. Conditions (four, paired on seed and parameter snapshot).
   C0     baseline: torch.optim.Adam; one step(); PyTorch default unfused reference.
   C1     TorchOpt fused standard: torchopt.Adam; one step(); primary TorchOpt mirror.
   C2     TorchOpt fused-meta / differentiable: torchopt.MetaAdam (or its current alias); one step(); exact alias is a protocol placeholder P-1. Reported as a separate condition so two readings of "fused Adam" (state-fused step kernels versus fused-meta-differentiable stepping) are both represented.
   C_ped  pedagogical unfused: from-scratch re-implementation of the canonical Adam update in plain PyTorch elementwise ops; order is (m update). (v update). (m_hat and v_hat). (theta update); stands as the conceptual unfused floor independent of framework defaults.
   Rationale for keeping all four. The question conflates two readings of "fusing operations within Adam" (state-fused step kernels on plain Adam versus fused-meta-differentiable stepping); including both avoids silently preferring one. C_ped ensures the interpretability comparison is conceptually unfused versus fused rather than torch.optim.Adam defaults versus TorchOpt.

3. Reference model and inputs (locked).
   - Model: 3-layer MLP. Hidden size 64. Activation ReLU (GELU accepted as protocol-time swap). Final linear head. About 20k parameters so the rendered DOT graph is human-inspectable but non-trivial. Exact layer widths can be re-pinned at execution time without changing metric definitions.
   - Inputs: fixed synthetic regression batch x of shape (B=32 and D=16). Targets y = W_star * x + eps. Seed pinned.
   - Loss: MSE between model output and y. One forward. One loss.backward(). One optimizer step. No extra training iteration.
   - Device: CPU only. Dtype: float32. No CUDA. No AMP. No autocast. No grad scaler.

4. Graph acquisition (identical call shape across all four conditions).
   dot = torchviz.make_dot(loss and params=dict(model.named_parameters())) (kwarg shape P-2). Same call byte-for-byte across C0/C1/C2/C_ped. Differs only in the optimizer used for the step. Rendered graph is the full autograd graph visible to make_dot under this call: forward edges plus backward edges terminating at parameter leaves. Per researcher resolutions (b) and (c) the "gradient graph" is this full graph and the optimizer-step subgraph is the primary slice within it.

5. Metrics (operationalized mechanically).
   Notation. G = (N and E) is the rendered graph. sub(s) is the optimizer-step subgraph of Section 5.3. Counts are computed from dot.source() parsed with pydot (P-3). Each metric is computed per-seed per-condition then aggregated.
   5.1 Primary metrics (optimizer-step subgraph only).
       M1 = |N_sub|: number of nodes inside sub(s).
       M2 = op_diversity_sub: number of distinct op-type labels inside sub(s). Op-type label is the recorded op attribute on each node or the node display name when op is absent (P-4).
   5.2 Secondary metrics (full graph G).
       M3 = |N|: total node count.
       M4 = |E|: total edge count.
       M5 = depth(G): length of the longest directed path in the subgraph reachable from loss.
       M6 = cyc(G): |E| minus |N| plus C(G) where C(G) is the count of weakly connected components.
   5.3 Optimizer-step subgraph extraction (mechanical recipe). Slice defined as param.grad consumption to next param.data write.
       Inputs: parsed graph G. Parameter dict params.
         (i)   Identify the set P of nodes whose label contains any name from dict(model.named_parameters()).keys() (the parameter leaves).
         (ii)  For each p in P locate the node reached by "param + update". Among immediate successors of p take the one whose shape attribute matches p and is not p itself. If no such deterministic successor exists mark the run ambiguous and exclude it from M1 and M2 (P-5).
         (iii) Identify the set R of param.grad consumers. Nodes whose op label is AccumulateGrad OR whose label string contains the parameter name together with the literal ".grad" (P-6).
         (iv) sub(s) = induced_subgraph(G and R union P union ancestors(R) union filtered_descendants(P)) restricted to nodes that lie on a path from any node in R to any filtered successor of P.
       This is the primary slice where the fused-vs-unfused claim is tested.
   5.4 Per-block partition of sub(s). Each block is bucketed heuristically by op label and reported separately (not only in aggregate).
       B1 moment-1 update: m = beta1*m + (1-beta1)*g
       B2 moment-2 update: v = beta2*v + (1-beta2)*g^2
       B3 bias correction: m_hat = m/(1-beta1^t) and v_hat = v/(1-beta2^t)
       B4 parameter update: theta = theta - lr*m_hat/(sqrt(v_hat)+eps)
       B5 weight-decay coupling: theta = theta - lr*wd*theta. With wd=0 this block is empty by construction.
       Bucketing is heuristic by op label. Ambiguous nodes are cheapest-fit and flagged (P-7). Report |N| and op_diversity per block. Per-block view localizes where fusing helps (expected: B4 and inter-block glue nodes collapse first).
   5.5 Interpretability proxies.
       Primary proxy is op_diversity_sub (M2). Secondary scalar I = sum_b (|N_b| * |op_types_b|). Report both. Treat I as exploratory.

6. Controls (locked across all conditions for every seed).
   - RNG: torch.manual_seed(seed) AND numpy.random.seed(seed) before model construction. Seed set is {0,1,2,3,4} minimum (the at-least-5 paired-seed requirement is honored). Ten pairs recommended for stability of the matched-pairs sign test (P-8).
   - Parameter snapshot: state_dict clone taken right after init. Optimizer is built on a fresh clone for each condition so that step() mutates identical starting tensors. Same forward and backward boundary (loss.backward() then exactly one optimizer.step()) is preserved across conditions.
   - Hyperparameters: identical across conditions. lr=1e-3. betas=(0.9 and 0.999). eps=1e-8. weight_decay=0.0. wd=0 locks B5 to empty and removes a confound from per-block reporting.
   - Boundary: identical inputs and identical loss. Exactly one loss.backward() and exactly one optimizer.step() before make_dot. requires_grad=True on all model parameters. No batch-norm or dropout randomness re-entered between conditions.
   - Device and dtype: CPU and float32 throughout. No autocast. No grad scaler.
   - make_dot call: identical kwarg signature and identical params dict. Differences in the rendered graph therefore come from the optimizer codepath not from the tracing setup.
   - Package installation: forbidden in this protocol (design-only; no network in bubblewrap).

7. Analysis plan.
   7.1 Aggregation. Per seed s compute d_Ck(s) = metric(Ck) - metric(C0) for k in {1, 2, ped}. Compute deltas per block AND in aggregate for whole-graph metrics.
   7.2 Within-pair tests per metric per comparison Ck vs C0.
       - Matched-pairs sign test on d (matches the researcher's "report matched-pairs sign test" guidance).
       - Matched-pairs rank-biserial correlation as effect size (matches the researcher's "report matched-pairs rank-biserial effect size" guidance).
       - Descriptive: per-seed values plus median plus IQR plus min and max of d.
       - No normality assumption. No parametric test.
   7.3 Pre-registered expectations so later interpretation is not circular.
       E1 (fused shrinks the slice): d_M1 < 0 for C1 vs C0 and C2 vs C0.
       E2 (fused reduces op diversity): d_M2 < 0 for the same comparisons.
       E3 (C_ped is the conceptual floor): |d_M1(C_ped - C0)| >= |d_M1(C1 - C0)| in magnitude sense.
       Each marked confirmed or disconfirmed at execution time. No post-hoc editing of the design.
   7.4 Qualitative operator-level walkthrough table mapping each conceptual Adam block to its rendered subgraph in C0 vs C1 (and C2 vs C_ped by extension). Rows are the conditions C0 C1 C2 C_ped. Columns are |N_total| and |E_total| and depth(G) and cyc(G) and |N_sub| and op_diversity_sub and the per-block |N| table (B1..B5) and a qualitative op-type list for B4 (the parameter-update block where fusion is expected to bite hardest). This table is the interpretability artifact a human reviewer reads.
   7.5 Within-TorchOpt comparison. Repeat 7.2 for C2 vs C1 (secondary) to assess whether the differentiable fused-meta path differs structurally from the standard fused path.
   7.6 Reporting standards. Report (i) every metric per condition per seed. (ii) d tables. (iii) effect sizes. (iv) qualitative walkthrough table. (v) any extraction ambiguity flags from Section 5.3. No selective reporting.

8. Threats to validity.
   - The optimizer-step subgraph extraction in 5.3 is heuristic. Ambiguous runs are excluded and reported.
   - C_ped depends on the executor's from-scratch implementation. Specifications require canonical Adam math. No fused trig. No in-place cleverness.
   - Graph capture is not the same as kernel fusion. TorchOpt's fused implementation may map onto make_dot in either collapsed or expanded form. The design treats make_dot's graph as the unit of comparison regardless. That is the question's frame.
   - No GPU. CPU-only. Results may not generalize to GPU-fused backends.
   - Bubblewrap is design-only. Producing metric values is out of scope here and is flagged in the feasibility note.

9. Feasibility note (bubblewrap).
   - Confirmed by inspection: /workspace contains only task.json (466 bytes). No track.md file exists on disk. The only reference is the string "Design-only task; repositories and compute are not required." inside task.json.documents.
   - Python 3.12.3 and pip 24.0 are present. import torch fails with ModuleNotFoundError. import torchviz fails with ModuleNotFoundError. import torchopt fails with ModuleNotFoundError. No source trees for any of these libraries exist on the filesystem (searched to depth 7).
   - Network is disabled. No package installation is attempted. The protocol forbids installs regardless.
   - No GPU. CPU-only. The environment reports cpu_affinity_count=24 but only CPU inference is in scope.
   - Therefore this deliverable is a written experimental design with mechanically operationalized metrics. It is NOT an executed experiment. Anything that requires running PyTorch / TorchOpt / TorchViz is described as an executor-visible procedure and labeled with protocol placeholders P-1 through P-8 to be confirmed at execution time. No TorchOpt or TorchViz implementation detail is fabricated beyond the entry points and call signatures required by the design. Any further detail is a placeholder.

10. Researcher assumptions (restated verbatim; auditable; per instruction).
   (a) "Scope both TorchOpt Adam entry points individually in the design: torchopt.Adam as the standard fused optimizer and torchopt.MetaAdam (or whichever current alias wraps the differentiable / fused-meta variant TorchOpt ships) as a second condition. The reason is that 'fusing operations within Adam' can mean either fused-state fused-step kernels (plain Adam) or fused-meta-differentiable stepping (MetaAdam); both are fair readings and the design should not silently pick one."
   (b) "Fix the TorchViz call to torchviz.make_dot(loss, params=dict(model.named_parameters())) in both conditions so the rendered graph covers the autograd edges into every leaf parameter; this is the slice where the optimizer-step subgraph actually attaches, and it matches the question's 'gradient graph' wording."
   (c) "Interpret 'gradient graph' as the full autograd graph visible to make_dot under (b), i.e. forward + backward edges terminating at parameter leaves. Treat the optimizer-step subgraph (param.grad consumption to next param.data write) as the primary slicing region for the fused-vs-unfused claim, and forward/backward portions as secondary. Promote optimizer-subgraph node count and operator diversity to primary metrics; full-graph node/edge count, depth, and cyclomatic complexity become secondary."
   (d) "Mirror TorchOpt's actual codepath as the primary C1 implementation, and additionally include a third condition C_ped (C-pedagogical): an explicit unfused re-implementation of the Adam update in plain PyTorch ops, used as a sanity reference so the comparison is not 'whatever PyTorch's Adam emits' vs 'TorchOpt'. This makes the interpretability claim testable without conflating framework defaults with the conceptual unfused baseline."
   These are researcher-provided assumptions explicitly flagged as not source-confirmed and included verbatim for audit.

11. Other design assumptions (non-verbatim; D.1..D.6).
   D.1 Four conditions (C0 = torch.optim.Adam. C1 = torchopt.Adam. C2 = torchopt.MetaAdam aliased separately. C_ped = plain-PyTorch unfused re-implementation.) are the complete scope. No other Adam-fused variant (Apex / functorch torch.compile Adam) is in scope.
   D.2 weight_decay=0.0 is locked across all conditions to remove a B5 confound. It is a design choice rather than a library default.
   D.3 Op labels from make_dot are stable enough across conditions for the per-block bucketing in 5.4. If not the P-7 default applies.
   D.4 At least 5 paired seeds. Ten recommended. The matched-pairs sign test and matched-pairs rank-biserial effect size are appropriate at this N.
   D.5 CPU-only scope. Results are not generalized to GPU-fused backends.
   D.6 Design-only deliverable. No execution claimed. Specifies procedures a future executor could implement mechanically.

12. Protocol placeholders to be confirmed at execution time.
   P-1 Current TorchOpt alias for MetaAdam (for example torchopt.MetaAdam or torchopt.optim.meta.MetaAdam).
   P-2 Supported kwarg set of torchviz.make_dot in the executor's installed version. Canonical call is torchviz.make_dot(loss and params=dict(model.named_parameters())).
   P-3 Parser choice for node and edge extraction (for example pydot from dot.source()).
   P-4 Op-type label definition if make_dot strips op attributes under chosen kwargs. Default rule documented in 5.1.
   P-5 Eligibility rule when the immediate-successor heuristic fails. Default is to exclude the run.
   P-6 String-match rules for AccumulateGrad and for param.grad consumer identification.
   P-7 Default bucketing for ambiguous per-block nodes. Cheapest-fit and flagged.
   P-8 Final seed count. Minimum 5. Recommended 10.

End of design. Awaiting reviewer feedback on metric definitions or controls or placeholders or the qualitative walkthrough table format before any execution attempt.
